text:
Samir: FYI - between 11:02 and 11:25 we saw sustained 3x GPU utilization in shared-pool-us-east-1, causing 95p latency to jump from 180ms -> 1.2s. probable noisy neighbor. infra-bot posted alerts.

Maya: saw a cascade of OOM evictions on node gpuship-45 right around 11:10. a bunch of small endpoints got preempted. :grimacing:

Infra Bot: ALERT: gpu_utilization > 90% on gpuship-45 (shared-pool-us-east-1) — 11:12 UTC. Auto-evict triggered.

Jordan: Can we confirm whether the tenant was running multi-turn chat with 8k context + streaming? that workload can blow up kv-cache and memory.

Samir: logs show a single tenant (tenant: acme-sim) with 30 concurrent streams using model: gpt-large-16k-q4. KV cache entries exploded.

Priya: acme-sim is on shared tier, they spiked due to a load test. they should have been in dedicated. we did not route them because they never hit the billing/dedicated rule.

Ankit: suggestion: add short-term burst isolation + eviction whitelist for critical hosted endpoints. also consider routing high-concurrency sessions to a capacitated fallback pool.

Maya: +1. We need a soft quota per-tenant on shared pools (concurrent streams, gpu_mem_bytes) to avoid single tenant saturating a node.

Samir: here's a quick router policy prototype I threw together:
```yaml
route: shared-us-east
  match: tenant.tier == "shared"
  soft_quota:
    concurrent_streams: 10
    gpu_mem_bytes: 28GiB
  on_violation:
    - action: throttle
    - action: route_to: dedicated-burst-us-east
    - action: notify: # infra team
```

Jordan: That looks sane. question: route_to dedicated-burst will increase cost if used frequently — we need a TTL and cost-accounting tag so finance knows which tenants get charged for burst routing.

Priya: agree. add a tag like `routing.charge:burst` and emit usage events to billing. we already emit model_token counts, just need per-route tagging.

Ankit: for now we can add a temporary mitigation: 1) tighten shared pool per-tenant concurrency to 8, 2) enable prefix KV cache pruning after 30m idle, 3) set router fallback to smaller model variant (gpt-medium-8k) before routing to paid burst.

Maya: can we do a canary rollout for the new router rule? target hostnames: dev- and staging-first, then 10% prod. I'd prefer not to touch all customers at once.

Samir: yep. I'll open a PR with the rule + canary flag. plan: 10% prod for 2 hours, monitor 95p latency and evictions. if evictions drop and SLOs are stable, ramp.

Infra Bot: NOTE: created incident ticket INF-2026-117 with logs and initial triage. assigned to Samir.

Jordan: Also let's document behavior when dedicated pools are full — currently router will fallback to best-effort shared, which is bad for the dedicated customer. we should prioritize SLAs: route dedicated->dedicated-fallback (throttled) not shared.

Priya: good catch. add a routing priority tree: dedicated > dedicated-fallback > shared-burst > shared. and set explicit evict policies so we don't silently degrade SLA'd tenants.

Samir: I'll include that in the PR. timeline: hotfix for soft quotas + canary router change today, longer term: enforce per-tenant resource accounting in the scheduler and implement a dedicated pool reservation UI in the console.

Maya: for postmortem: quantify customer impact (which requests slowed, which retried), estimate cost delta if we had routed to dedicated-burst for the full spike. send to cs + finance.

Ankit: also check network egress saturation on that rack — if KV cache push/pulls are amplified it can cause tail latency. I saw RPC retries in the same timeframe.

Samir: noted. adding network checks to the runbook.

Jordan: thanks all. if anyone sees recurring pattern, tag the tenant and we can proactively offer a dedicated pool with a trial discount. saving SLO > paying for dedicated. :money_with_wings:

Maya: PR link incoming in ~30m. I'll be on standby for the canary. :thumbsup:
